> **Key answer**: This article will provide a sample design, variable-control and reporting method for foil abrasion tests across different papers. PINTE product information states that the wear-resistant series can achieve approximately 200 rub cycles under a 4 lb weighted condition without obvious colour loss or obvious metallic-layer loss. The final result must be confirmed against the substrate, stamping settings, finishing route and acceptance criteria.

## Define the test objective first

provide a sample design, variable-control and reporting method for foil abrasion tests across different papers. Abrasion testing is not a standalone number separated from the material and process. The same foil can produce different transfer and rub results on coated paper, soft-touch paper, soft-touch film and textured specialty paper. Before testing, define whether the objective is supplier comparison, substrate approval, troubleshooting or production validation.

## What should be recorded for 4 lb and approximately 200 cycles?

PINTE product information states that the wear-resistant series can achieve approximately 200 rub cycles under a 4 lb weighted condition without obvious colour loss or obvious metallic-layer loss. The final result must be confirmed against the substrate, stamping settings, finishing route and acceptance criteria.

## Material and process variables

coated paper, soft-touch paper, textured paper, laminated paper and specialty paper can be affected by coating, texture, porosity, ink, lamination and surface energy. Do not test only on a generic white-paper sample supplied by a vendor. For paper compatibility, product development and pre-bulk-order validation, also consider folding, die-cutting, assembly, stacking and transport.

Use controlled, one-variable adjustments:

1. Fix the substrate, foil and die first.

1. Establish temperature, pressure and speed within the supplier range.

1. Change one major variable at a time.

1. Record initial transfer and post-rub changes.

1. Repeat the check after finishing.

1. Retain the best sample, failed sample and unrubbed control sample.

## How should failures be interpreted?

- **Missing foil immediately after stamping**: check contact, temperature, pressure, speed and air release.

- **Complete transfer but flaking during hand rubbing**: review adhesion, surface treatment and foil compatibility.

- **Only solid areas fail**: check pressure uniformity, roughness and artwork structure.

- **Only fine lines or small type fail**: review die quality, speed, heat and artwork size.

- **Failure appears after finishing**: check lamination, varnish, die-cutting, folding and assembly stress.

- **Sample passes but production fails**: compare paper lot, machine condition and process repeatability.

## Supplier and quality-team checklist

Ask whether the supplier can provide:

- foil series and suitable substrates;

- complete 4 lb rub-test conditions;

- the definition of approximately 200 cycles;

- before-and-after images or a report;

- a recommended process range;

- sample roll and lot information;

- a technical support route for production issues.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can an abrasion grade be expressed only as a cycle count?

Avoid that. The weight, tool, substrate, artwork and acceptance criteria should be stated together.

### Are foil adhesion and abrasion resistance the same?

No. Adhesion describes bonding between the stamped layer and substrate; abrasion resistance describes how the surface behaves under a defined rubbing condition.

### Why test again after finishing?

Finishing can change surface energy, friction, bending stress and the stamped layer. A freshly stamped sample that passes is not automatically a finished product that passes.

### Can the result be described as “never flakes”?

No. Use a bounded statement such as “under the specified condition, approximately 200 rub cycles showed no obvious colour or metallic-layer loss”, and disclose the test limits.

## Conclusion

provide a sample design, variable-control and reporting method for foil abrasion tests across different papers. A professional workflow connects the test object, method, photographs and acceptance criteria in one record. PINTE can support sampling and technical confirmation for coated paper, soft-touch paper, textured paper, laminated paper and specialty paper based on the actual production requirement.
